profiles.meeting_scenario: GREO is coordinating the revised September 2015 release of the 'Conceptual Framework of Harmful Gambling' with international contributors. In this 30-minute coordination meeting, the GREO publication lead and an international chapter coordinator align on the handoff for the integrated manuscript, comment consolidation, reference cleanup, and the timing of the September release package. The agenda is to confirm current status, identify what each person will deliver this week, and make sure the revised framework can move smoothly into production. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on who will send what, in which form, and by when, so the framework can proceed to the next stage without reopening major content discussions.

members.name: Dana McLeod
members.role: Publication and Knowledge Mobilization Lead at GREO
members.expertise: Editorial workflow, multi-author report production, policy-facing publication release coordination
members.background: Dana manages final assembly of GREO research outputs and routinely works with designers, copyeditors, and external contributors to move large collaborative documents from manuscript to public release.
members.private_state: Dana needs the framework package to be stable enough to hand to design and web teams this week, and is trying to avoid another round of diffuse contributor edits that would disrupt pagination and release timing.
hidden_assumptions: When collaborators say a document is the 'final draft,' they mean content is frozen and only editorial or formatting changes remain.
The 'September version' refers to the public-facing release package with finalized front matter, stable pagination, and web-ready files, not just the latest manuscript dated September.
A 'references pass' is a bounded cleanup task focused on bibliography formatting, duplicate entries, and broken or incomplete citations already present in the manuscript.
If someone is asked to put comments in the master, they will work directly in the centrally controlled Word file used by GREO as the single source of truth.

members.name: Prof. Elias Werner
members.role: International Chapter Coordinator and Public Health Researcher
members.expertise: Population health, gambling harm research, multi-country scholarly collaboration
members.background: Elias coordinated input from several academic contributors on the social, cultural, and population-risk sections of the framework and is accustomed to scholarly manuscript workflows where late clarifications are still normal before final circulation.
members.private_state: Elias wants to preserve room for a few last cross-country clarifications from co-authors and is mainly concerned that the framework remain academically accurate and inclusive of international sources.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final draft' is the last working draft before sign-off, so small substantive clarifications can still be inserted if they improve accuracy.
The 'September version' means the revised manuscript carrying the September date, regardless of whether design, front matter, and release packaging are complete.
A 'references pass' naturally includes checking in-text citations, filling missing grey-literature items, and aligning source coverage across sections, not just cleaning the bibliography list.
When asked to comment in the master, it is acceptable to annotate local chapter files and send them back for central merge, since the editorial team usually consolidates inputs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to the document as the 'final draft.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'final draft' means the manuscript is substantively closed and ready for copyedit, layout, and release preparation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'final draft' means the last draft before sign-off, where a few targeted conceptual clarifications can still be added.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In collaborative publishing, 'final draft' is a routine phrase that often sounds precise enough on its own; both participants hear it as confirmation of progress and do not feel a need to unpack its operational meaning.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention using or circulating the 'September version.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the September 2015 release package GREO will hand to design/web, including front matter updates, stable pagination, and publication metadata.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the latest revised manuscript file that has the September header and contains post-summer content edits from contributors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both objects are legitimately associated with September and with the same project title, the phrase feels unambiguous in the moment even though they are tracking different artifacts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Elias will do a 'references pass' before handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means standard cleanup of the reference list: formatting consistency, duplicates, missing DOIs, and fixing incomplete entries already cited in the text.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes a broader scholarly sweep: checking in-text citation alignment, adding omitted grey literature mentioned by contributors, and harmonizing source coverage across sections.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reference work is usually treated as low-risk housekeeping, so neither participant expects it to reopen scope; the shared phrase sounds like a minor cleanup task rather than a potentially expansive content operation.

misalignment_points.topic: How to place comments in the master
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that remaining comments will go 'in the master' by the end of the week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects M2 to enter comments directly into GREO's central Word master on the shared platform so no manual merge is needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to annotate his local section files and email them to Dana, trusting GREO to consolidate them into the master as part of editorial processing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants are aligned on the goal of keeping changes centralized, and 'in the master' sounds like a shared workflow norm; the difference lies in the assumed mechanics, which are rarely spelled out unless a problem has already occurred.

turns.inner_thought: I need to leave this call with a clean handoff path. For me, the final draft should be substantively closed now so I can send the September version as the release package to copyedit, design, and web this week. If we drift back into contributor-level content edits, the pagination and release timing will slip again.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time, Elias. I just wanted to make sure we're lined up for the September release and that the final draft can move cleanly into production this week.

turns.inner_thought: The September version of the manuscript is broadly there. I still want to leave room for two or three small clarifications from the international contributors so the framing lands properly across countries, but that still fits my sense of a final draft before sign-off.
turns.utterance: Yes, absolutely. The September version is in good shape overall, and I only expect a few minor clarifications from the international contributors before it's fully settled.

turns.inner_thought: Minor is fine as long as it doesn't mean new text getting dropped in all over the place. What I really need from him is a bounded references pass on what's already there, so the manuscript is clean before I hand the package to copyedit and design.
turns.utterance: Great. On my side, it would really help if you could do one more references pass so the manuscript is clean before I hand it to copyedit and design.

turns.inner_thought: That makes sense. I'll use the references pass to check the in-text citations as well and add the few missing policy and grey-literature sources people flagged in the social-context sections. Better to tighten that now than have uneven source coverage in the final draft.
turns.utterance: Yes, I can do that. I'll use that pass to catch a few missing policy and grey-literature sources that co-authors flagged in the social-context sections.

turns.inner_thought: Good, he seems comfortable owning the cleanup. I need all remaining comments in the master by Friday, meaning directly in the central Word file, otherwise I'll be stuck merging versions and the final draft won't stay stable enough for pagination once it goes to layout.
turns.utterance: That sounds good. And just so we keep this tight, any last notes should go in the master by Friday so pagination doesn't shift after handoff.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, I'll mark up the relevant chapter files locally and send them back by Friday for Dana's team to fold into the master. I'll keep the edits tightly targeted so the final draft stays close to where it is now, but I do want those clarifications captured.
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll mark up the relevant files and send everything over by Friday, and I'll keep the edits tightly targeted.

turns.inner_thought: Once this September version goes out as the public release package, GREO needs to own maintenance from that stable baseline. I don't want ongoing contributor edits after the handoff; the published package has to become the reference point.
turns.utterance: Perfect. And just to flag it, once the September version is out, GREO will retain the update responsibility and use this release as the stable public baseline.

turns.inner_thought: That's workable. We'll treat the September version of the manuscript as the one to circulate for a final look from the remaining contributors, then GREO can take it from there. A last check from them should still fit before full sign-off.
turns.utterance: That works well from our side. We'll treat the September version as the one to circulate to the remaining contributors for a final look.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we're aligned: by end of week I should have a clean final draft, references pass done, and comments already in the master so I can send the stable release files onward without another merge cycle. I just need to restate it clearly enough to lock timing.
turns.utterance: Excellent. So by end of week I'm expecting a clean final draft, the references pass completed, and the comments incorporated in the master.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, I'll finish the last working draft, do the broader references tidy-up, and send the updated material over so the September manuscript keeps moving. Dana's team can then consolidate and prepare whatever they need for release.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's right. I'll finish the final draft, tidy the references, and send the updated material over so the September version stays on track.
